cls: Recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor (topical wound-healing agent)
pharm: Recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor (rhPDGF-BB) topical gel that promotes chemotactic recruitment and proliferation of wound-repair cells and granulation tissue formation in diabetic foot ulcers.
quick: Thin layer applied once daily; length calculated from ulcer size
No human data; use only if clearly needed
Ulcer size reduction at 10 weeks; malignancy risk
summary: Becaplermin (Regranex 0.01% gel) is a recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor applied topically as an adjunct to good ulcer care for lower-extremity diabetic neuropathic ulcers that extend into subcutaneous tissue or beyond and have adequate blood supply. It carries a BOXED WARNING for increased mortality from malignancy in patients who used three or more tubes. It is contraindicated over a known neoplasm at the application site.
indications: Lower extremity diabetic neuropathic ulcers that extend into subcutaneous tissue or beyond and have an adequate blood supply, as an adjunct to good ulcer care practices

dosage.c: Diabetic neuropathic foot ulcer (15 g tube)
dosage.n: Length in inches = ulcer length x width x 0.6; length in cm = ulcer length x width / 4

dosage.d: Adjust amount as ulcer dimensions change
dosage.n: Reassess if no ~30% size reduction by 10 weeks; stop if not healed by 20 weeks

admin: Measure the ulcer and calculate the gel length using the size-based formula
Squeeze the calculated amount onto a clean firm surface (e.g., wax paper)
Apply an even thin layer (~1/16 inch) over the ulcer with a clean cotton swab or tongue depressor
Cover with a saline-moistened gauze dressing for ~12 hours, then remove, rinse with saline or water, and cover with a fresh moist (non-gel) dressing for the rest of the day
Apply once daily; maintain strict non-weight-bearing/off-loading regimen
Wash hands before and after; do not exceed 20 weeks of therapy
moa: Recombinant human platelet-derived growth factor (rhPDGF-BB) that promotes chemotactic recruitment of cells involved in wound repair, stimulates their proliferation, and enhances formation of granulation tissue, thereby accelerating healing of diabetic neuropathic ulcers.

absolute: Known neoplasm(s) at the site(s) of application
Known hypersensitivity to becaplermin or any component (e.g., parabens)
relative: Wounds that close by primary intention
Use in patients with known malignancy (weigh benefit/risk carefully)

preg: No adequate human data; animal reproduction studies have not been conducted. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether becaplermin is excreted in human milk; exercise caution in nursing mothers.
renal: Not applicable; topical use with minimal systemic absorption.
hepatic: Not applicable; topical use with minimal systemic absorption.

minor: Interaction with other topical agents applied to the ulcer site is not known; avoid co-application

serious: Malignancy (reported in postmarketing surveillance, distant from application sites)
rare: Cellulitis or local infection of the ulcer
emergency: Signs of new or progressing malignancy (unexplained weight loss, new masses)

monitoring: Ulcer size and healing - expect approximately 30% reduction by 10 weeks
Complete healing by 20 weeks (reassess therapy if not achieved)
Local signs of infection or adverse reaction
Signs/symptoms of malignancy in patients using multiple tubes
counsel: Apply exactly as directed once daily; review the Medication Guide and Instructions for Use
Keep the ulcer area off-loaded and maintain strict non-weight-bearing as instructed
Store the tube refrigerated and do not freeze; do not use after the expiration date
This medicine may increase the risk of cancer death in people who use 3 or more tubes; tell your doctor about any history of cancer
Report any new lumps, unexplained weight loss, or worsening of the wound
pk: Promotes granulation over days to weeks
Once-daily application; treat up to 20 weeks
Refrigerate 2-8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze
pearls: BOXED WARNING: increased rate of mortality secondary to malignancy in patients who used 3 or more tubes of becaplermin gel
Adjunct only - effective ulcer care including debridement, infection control, and off-loading is essential
Ineffective for pressure ulcers and venous stasis ulcers
Requires adequate blood supply to the ulcer to work
Gel amount is recalculated as the ulcer dimensions change
missed: Apply the missed dose when remembered; if it is nearly time for the next daily dose, skip the missed one. Do not apply extra gel to make up.
overdose: No data on the effects of overdose; systemic toxicity from topical use is unlikely. Manage any local reaction supportively.
